title: GET /api/auth/google — initiate Google OAuth flow
description: Set up Google OAuth 2.0 login using Passport.js. User clicks 'Sign in with Google', is redirected to Google, and returns to the app authenticated with access + refresh tokens.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/auth/google redirects to Google OAuth consent screen
On success: creates or updates user record, issues tokens, redirects to FRONTEND_URL/auth/callback?token=ACCESS_TOKEN
New Google users are created with no password_hash

steps.details: npm install passport passport-google-oauth20. npm install -D @types/passport @types/passport-google-oauth20.

Create server/src/config/passport.ts. Configure GoogleStrategy with clientID (GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID), clientSecret (GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET), callbackURL ('/api/auth/google/callback'). In the verify callback: find user by google_id OR email. If found, update google_id if missing. If not found, create new user with name, email, google_id from profile. Return user.

In auth router: GET /google → passport.authenticate('google', { scope: ['profile', 'email'], session: false }). GET /google/callback → passport.authenticate(..., { session: false, failureRedirect: FRONTEND_URL/login?error=oauth_failed }) then issue tokens, set refresh cookie, redirect to FRONTEND_URL/auth/callback?token=ACCESS_TOKEN.
In server/src/index.ts, import passport config, call passport.initialize() middleware, app.use(passport.initialize()). No session middleware needed (session: false).
Open http://localhost:3000/api/auth/google in a browser. Complete Google sign-in. Verify redirect to FRONTEND_URL/auth/callback?token=... Verify user created in DB with google_id set.

technicalNotes: Use session: false in Passport to avoid needing session middleware
Pass access token in redirect URL query param — frontend reads it and stores in memory
Google OAuth requires HTTPS in production; localhost works in development
